claim: Robert Goddard launches the world's first liquid-fueled rocket at Auburn, Massachusetts.
sources: NASA History Office (nasa.gov); Smithsonian NASM

claim: NBC launches as the first permanent national radio broadcasting network in the US.
sources: Library of Congress NBC research guide (guides.loc.gov/nbc); Encyclopaedia Britannica

claim: Charles Lindbergh completes the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight (New York–Paris) in the Spirit of St. Louis.
sources: Smithsonian Pioneers of Flight (pioneersofflight.si.edu); EBSCO Research Starters

claim: Philo Farnsworth demonstrates the first working all-electronic television image transmission.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica; Television Academy Interviews

claim: The Jazz Singer premieres as the first feature-length film with synchronized recorded dialogue, launching the sound-film era.
sources: Library of Congress National Film Preservation Board; Encyclopaedia Britannica

claim: The Northern Expedition ends with nominal national reunification under the Nationalist (KMT) government seated at Nanjing.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (China: The Northern Expedition); Encyclopedia.com

claim: Academia Sinica (中央研究院), China's national academy of sciences, is founded at Nanjing.
sources: Nature 136, 208 (1935), 'Scientific Research in China: The Academia Sinica'; Encyclopaedia Britannica

claim: The Central Bank of China is established in Shanghai as the Nationalist government's central bank.
sources: Encyclopedia.com (Bank of China / Central Bank of China); academic histories of the Nanjing Decade

claim: Pei Wenzhong discovers the first Peking Man (Homo erectus) skullcap at Zhoukoudian.
sources: Encyclopedia.com (Pei Wenzhong); Springer Encyclopedia of Global Archaeology

claim: China completes the restoration of tariff autonomy as the last major power accedes, ending foreign control over Chinese customs tariff rates. Anchor justification: treaty sequence US 1928 -> most powers by end-1928 -> new tariff effective Feb 1929 -> Japan (last major power) 6 May 1930; anchored to the 1930 completion.
sources: Ching-Chun Wang, 'How China Recovered Tariff Autonomy' (Annals AAPSS, 1930); US State Dept Foreign Relations (FRUS 1928, Sino-US tariff treaty)

claim: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto at Lowell Observatory, the first trans-Neptunian object found.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (Clyde Tombaugh); New Mexico State University Tombaugh exhibit

claim: Liang Shuming establishes the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute at Zouping, a landmark rural-reconstruction and mass-education experiment.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (Liang Shuming); academic studies of the Republican Rural Reconstruction Movement (ANU Press / ResearchGate)

claim: The Empire State Building is completed in New York City, then the tallest building in the world (381 m).
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica; ASCE Metropolitan Section landmark record

claim: Ernest Lawrence builds the first working cyclotron at Berkeley, enabling particle acceleration.
sources: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory history; American Physical Society (APS News, 'June 1931: Lawrence and the First Cyclotron')

claim: China's 'abolish the tael, adopt the yuan' reform standardizes the silver dollar (yuan) as the national monetary unit, replacing the tael.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (tael); LSE Economic History working paper (Chinese Monetary Integration, WP283)

claim: The Tennessee Valley Authority is established, a federal authority for regional electrification and river development.
sources: US National Archives (Milestone Documents: TVA Act); TVA official history (tva.com)

claim: The Glass–Steagall Banking Act creates federal deposit insurance (FDIC) and separates commercial and investment banking.
sources: Federal Reserve History (federalreservehistory.org, Banking Act of 1933); Cornell Legal Information Institute

claim: The fabi (法币) currency reform abandons the silver standard and unifies a managed national paper currency.
sources: Ho, Tai-kuang, 'China's 1935 Fiat Money Reform' (NTU Economics); 'The Fabi and the End of the Global Silver Era, 1933-1937' (academic)

claim: The Chinese Communist Party's Red Army completes the Long March, consolidating Mao Zedong's leadership and the CCP's survival.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (Long March); Columbia University Asia for Educators

claim: The Social Security Act establishes national old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.
sources: US Social Security Administration (ssa.gov/history/35act.html); Encyclopaedia Britannica

claim: Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is completed, then the world's largest concrete structure and hydroelectric dam.
sources: Herbert Hoover Presidential Library (hoover.archives.gov); Yale Energy History (FDR Boulder Dam dedication, Sept 30 1935)

claim: Wallace Carothers's team at DuPont first synthesizes nylon, the first fully synthetic polymer fiber.
sources: Science History Institute (Wallace Hume Carothers); EBSCO Research Starters (Carothers Invents Nylon)

claim: The Douglas DC-3 makes its first flight, becoming the airliner that made passenger air travel commercially viable.
sources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum (Douglas DC-3); This Day in Aviation

claim: The Canton-Hankow (Yuehan) Railway is completed, linking Guangzhou to Wuhan as a major north-south trunk line.
sources: P.A. Crush, 'Glimpse of Chinese Railway History' (Canton-Hankow Railway); contemporary record of the first through train, 6 Sep 1936 (Historical Photographs of China / Gwulo)

claim: The Qiantang River Bridge at Hangzhou, chief-engineered by Mao Yisheng, opens as the first modern double-deck road-and-rail bridge designed and built by Chinese engineers.
sources: Structurae engineering structures database (Qiantang River Bridge, 1937); Zhejiang provincial government record (ezhejiang.gov.cn)

claim: The Golden Gate Bridge opens in San Francisco, then the world's longest suspension-bridge main span.
sources: Library of Congress (Today in History, May 27); Encyclopaedia Britannica (Golden Gate Bridge)

claim: The National Southwestern Associated University (Xinan Lianda) forms in Kunming, merging Peking, Tsinghua, and Nankai universities to preserve higher education through the war.
sources: Stanford University Press, 'Lianda: A Chinese University in War and Revolution'; standard references

claim: The Chinese Industrial Cooperatives ('Gung Ho') movement organizes decentralized wartime production across the interior.
sources: University of Massachusetts Amherst archives (Indusco); Victoria Univ Wellington studies of the Chinese Industrial Cooperatives

claim: The Yunnan section of the Burma Road (Kunming to Wanting at the Burmese border, ~960 km), built by an estimated 200,000 Chinese laborers under Nationalist direction, opens to motor traffic in 1938. [Alt anchor: formal completion sometimes dated 1939; both recorded. Narrowed to the Chinese-built Yunnan section per batch-3 ruling.]
sources: Wikipedia (Burma Road); World War II Database (ww2db.com); The Irrawaddy ('On This Day')

claim: Chester Carlson produces the first xerographic image, inventing electrophotography (later Xerox copying).
sources: American Physical Society (aps.org, '22 Oct 1938: Invention of Xerography'); University of Rochester archives

claim: Hewlett-Packard is founded in Palo Alto, an origin point of what became Silicon Valley.
sources: Stanford University (engineering.stanford.edu, HP history); EBSCO Research Starters

claim: Enrico Fermi's team achieves the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction (Chicago Pile-1).
sources: Argonne National Laboratory; Los Alamos National Laboratory (Chicago Pile-1)

claim: Grand Coulee Dam on the Columbia River is completed, the largest concrete structure and hydroelectric plant in the US.
sources: US Bureau of Reclamation records; Encyclopaedia Britannica

claim: The US and UK relinquish extraterritorial rights in China by treaty, ending a century of the 'unequal treaties'.
sources: US State Dept Foreign Relations (FRUS 1943, China); Cambridge, Modern Asian Studies (extraterritoriality negotiations of 1943)

claim: US pharmaceutical firms achieve deep-tank fermentation mass production of penicillin, enabling the first antibiotic at scale.
sources: American Chemical Society National Historic Chemical Landmark (penicillin deep-tank fermentation); USDA ARS (Peoria NRRL)

claim: US wartime industrial mobilization mass-produces ships and aircraft at unprecedented scale (Liberty ships, tens of thousands of aircraft).
sources: The National WWII Museum (Arsenal of Democracy); US wartime production records via GlobalSecurity (~300,000 aircraft, ~2,700 Liberty ships)

claim: The Bretton Woods conference establishes the IMF and the framework for the World Bank, anchoring the postwar monetary order.
sources: IMF/World Bank archives (Bretton Woods, July 1944); US State Dept Office of the Historian

claim: The GI Bill (Servicemen's Readjustment Act) funds mass higher education and home ownership for returning veterans.
sources: US National Archives (Servicemen's Readjustment Act, 22 Jun 1944); Encyclopaedia Britannica

claim: China becomes a founding member of the United Nations and a permanent member of the Security Council.
sources: United Nations records (UN Charter founding members, June 1945); standard references

claim: ENIAC, the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, becomes operational.
sources: University of Pennsylvania (Penn Today, ENIAC); Computer History Museum

claim: The Manhattan Project achieves the first nuclear detonation (Trinity test), demonstrating engineered nuclear fission at scale.
sources: US Department of Energy (energy.gov, Trinity Site); Los Alamos National Laboratory

claim: Vannevar Bush's report 'Science, the Endless Frontier' sets the blueprint for federal funding of basic research (leading to the NSF).
sources: Smithsonian Institution (report record); National Science Foundation historical accounts

claim: Bell Labs invents the point-contact transistor (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley), foundation of all modern electronics.
sources: Computer History Museum (Silicon Engine); IEEE / Engineering & Technology History Wiki (Bell Labs transistor milestone)

claim: Chuck Yeager pilots the Bell X-1 to the first crewed supersonic flight, breaking the sound barrier.
sources: US Air Force Historical Support Division (afhistory.af.mil); NASA

claim: Levittown, New York begins mass-produced suburban housing, a template for postwar American suburbanization.
sources: Encyclopedia.com (Levittown); EBSCO Research Starters

claim: The Marshall Plan (European Recovery Program) begins large-scale US-funded reconstruction of Western Europe.
sources: US National Archives (Milestone Documents: Marshall Plan, Apr 1948); Congressional Research Service R45079

claim: Claude Shannon publishes 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication', founding information theory.
sources: Shannon, C.E., 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication', Bell System Technical Journal 27 (1948); IEEE Xplore reprint

claim: The People's Republic of China is founded, ending decades of civil war and fragmentation on the mainland.
sources: Taylor & Francis academic (Mao Proclaims the Founding of the PRC, 1 Oct 1949); US State Dept Office of the Historian

claim: The US leads the founding of NATO, the postwar transatlantic security institution.
sources: NATO official founding records (nato.int); US State Dept Office of the Historian

claim: The Marriage Law of 1950 bans arranged and child marriage and establishes new legal rights for women.
sources: LSE Economic History (Mao, marriage and modernization); UC Press, Revolutionizing the Family

claim: Nationwide Land Reform redistributes land from landlords to peasants under the 1950 Agrarian Reform Law. [Magnitude (official/standard estimate): ~700 million mu (~46.7M ha) redistributed; recorded, not independently re-measured.]
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (Agrarian Reform Law 1950); ChinaKnowledge.de

claim: The new government halts hyperinflation and stabilizes the renminbi, restoring monetary order.
sources: Springer, 'A Novel End to the Big Inflation in China in 1950'; Adam Tooze (Chartbook)

claim: UNIVAC I is delivered as the first commercially produced electronic computer in the US.
sources: Computer History Museum; US Census Bureau (census.gov)

claim: The Patriotic Health Campaign mobilizes mass sanitation and disease-control drives nationwide.
sources: Frontiers in Public Health (2026); Boston University (Elizabeth Perry lecture)

claim: The US detonates 'Ivy Mike', the first full-scale thermonuclear (hydrogen) device.
sources: US Atomic Energy Commission / Dept of Energy records; Encyclopaedia Britannica

claim: The First Five-Year Plan begins Soviet-aided heavy industrialization built around 156 key projects. [Event (plan launched 1953) established; the 156-project count (~150 built) and output magnitudes rest on official/planning data - independently discussed but not independently measured.]
sources: Business History Conference (Engineering the Socialist World); Encyclopaedia Britannica (China: transition to socialism)

claim: China conducts its first modern national census, counting roughly 583 million people. [Conflicting figures recorded: official count 582.6M (1953) vs the prior ~450M League of Nations 1933 estimate; G. Cressey questioned the count as inflated, though later scholarship assessed ~100% coverage.]
sources: Cambridge, Journal of Asian Studies ('The 1953 Chinese Census in Perspective'); Wikipedia (1953 Chinese census)

claim: The NTSC color television standard is adopted, launching compatible color broadcasting in the US.
sources: US National Archives (FCC color-TV records); IEEE / Engineering & Technology History Wiki

claim: The first Constitution of the PRC is adopted and the first National People's Congress convenes.
sources: Cornell eCommons (1954 PRC Constitution text/analysis); ChinaKnowledge.de

claim: USS Nautilus is commissioned as the world's first nuclear-powered submarine.
sources: US Naval History and Heritage Command; American Physical Society

claim: Bell Labs demonstrates the first practical silicon solar cell.
sources: American Physical Society; IEEE / Engineering & Technology History Wiki

claim: Qian Xuesen returns from the US to China, seeding the country's missile and later space programs.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (Qian Xuesen); US Naval Institute (Naval History)

claim: Jonas Salk's inactivated polio vaccine is licensed after mass field trials, curbing a feared epidemic disease.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica; University of Michigan School of Public Health

claim: Ray Kroc launches the McDonald's franchise system, a template for standardized mass-service industry.
sources: Emory University Goizueta Business Library; Time archive

claim: The First Automobile Works produces the Jiefang CA-10 truck, the first motor vehicle manufactured in China.
sources: Wikipedia (FAW Jiefang); CarNewsChina; Truck Encyclopedia

claim: The 'socialist transformation' of industry and commerce is completed, converting private enterprise to public/joint ownership.
sources: Project MUSE, 'Surviving Socialism'; Encyclopaedia Britannica (China: the transition to socialism, 1953-57)

claim: The Federal-Aid Highway Act launches the Interstate Highway System, the largest US public-works program.
sources: US House of Representatives History, Art & Archives; Cornell Legal Information Institute

claim: IBM ships the RAMAC 305, the first computer with a moving-head hard disk drive.
sources: Computer History Museum (Storage Engine); IBM / EDN records

claim: The Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opens, the first bridge to span the Yangtze, carrying rail and road.
sources: Structurae engineering database; Taylor & Francis, History and Technology ('Sino-Soviet cooperation... Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge')
